title: How a Large IT Consulting Company Works with Quantum - Quantum Computing Report
gist: CGI, a ~90,000-consultant IT integrator, sells quantum as a systems-integration and hybrid AI-classical-quantum service, with optimization (D-Wave partnership, US Defense Logistics Agency R&D) and post-quantum cryptography migration as the main entry points.

insights.claim: CGI, an IT consulting firm with roughly 90,000 consultants, does not build quantum computers but connects clients' complex use cases to third-party quantum hardware and tools.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Systems integrators are a hardware-agnostic, low-capex way to play quantum commercialization.
insights.locator: A Commercial, Pragmatic Approach to Quantum

insights.claim: CGI accesses many quantum providers, both annealing and gate-based, through partnerships and AWS and Azure subscriptions, so it can match hardware to each client problem.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Cloud marketplaces are the distribution channel through which integrators reach multiple quantum vendors.
insights.locator: A Commercial, Pragmatic Approach to Quantum

insights.claim: CGI reports a large recent rise in client demand for applied quantum use cases, whereas interest was largely exploratory a few years ago.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Enterprise quantum demand is shifting from exploration toward applied projects, a sign of market maturation.
insights.locator: While interest in quantum technology was largely exploratory

insights.claim: Mature hardware-vendor SDKs have lowered the barrier to entry so client teams with basic Python knowledge can begin exploring quantum use cases, and executive familiarity with quantum basics, like generative AI before it, lets consultants skip introductions.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Falling adoption friction supports faster pilot cycles and favors vendors with strong software ecosystems.
insights.locator: Much like the accelerated adoption of generative AI

insights.claim: Moving quantum from proof-of-concept to production is mainly a systems-integration problem: quantum algorithms must be woven into decades-old architectures, taking inputs from legacy data systems and outputting to familiar dashboards and reports.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Value capture in quantum may accrue to integration and services layers, not only to qubit makers.
insights.locator: Bridging the Gap: Systems Integration and Agentic AI

insights.claim: CGI treats AI as a bridge to quantum, not a competitor: an agentic digital workforce parses legacy IT, reverse-engineers classical logic, splits tasks, and routes suitable sub-tasks to quantum computers.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Hybrid AI-quantum orchestration is a likely product pattern; watch for it in integrator offerings.
insights.locator: Artificial intelligence plays a critical supporting role

insights.claim: Adopting quantum optimization requires retiring existing classical optimization models that internal teams invested heavily in, creating organizational change friction.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Sunk-cost and change-management barriers can slow enterprise conversion of pilots to production.

insights.claim: A production workload differs by architecture: annealers can run continuous background optimizations, while gate-based production may be just a research team routinely running targeted simulations within a larger workflow.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Near-term production revenue looks different for annealing versus gate-based vendors.

insights.claim: Optimization problems drive the bulk of CGI's quantum engagements, aligned with logistics, manufacturing and healthcare challenges.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Optimization via annealing is the leading near-term commercial quantum use case.
insights.locator: Strategic Alliances and High-Value Use Cases

insights.claim: CGI recently formalized a partnership with D-Wave to use its optimization tools and annealers, described as capable of 99% uptime, for continuous background re-optimization in dynamic production environments.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: A large integrator channel is a positive commercial signal for D-Wave.
insights.locator: CGI recently formalized a partnership with D-Wave

insights.claim: CGI Federal established a fiscal year 2027 R&D agreement with the US Defense Logistics Agency to commercialize quantum for warehouse management, reverse supply chain disposition and contested logistics, working from an onshore delivery center in Knoxville, Tennessee.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Defense logistics is an emerging government demand pocket for quantum optimization.
insights.locator: In the public sector, CGI Federal

insights.claim: Minor optimizations to delivery routes or supply chain logic in defense logistics can yield a 10% reduction in delivery costs and lower maintenance overhead.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: A concrete but unsourced ROI figure; treat as a marketing-grade benchmark.

insights.claim: Paint and other materials manufacturers are exploring quantum simulation of material degradation to accelerate testing that would otherwise need lengthy lab work, showing early traction in computational chemistry.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Chemistry and materials simulation is an early-stage second use case beyond optimization.

insights.claim: Post-quantum cryptography is a significant driver of overall quantum interest, and for many organizations security rather than optimization is the first entry point into quantum.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: PQC migration spending is a near-term demand wedge for security and consulting vendors.
insights.locator: Security, Sovereignty, and the Post-Quantum On-Ramp

insights.claim: CGI helps clients replace legacy systems with NIST-approved PQC algorithms, a process that often requires locating where cryptography is buried across large enterprise data estates.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Cryptographic inventory and discovery is a key work stream in PQC migrations.

insights.claim: PQC mapping work leads clients to ask what else quantum computers can do given they can break RSA, converting defensive security conversations into offensive business use cases.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: PQC engagements can seed broader quantum application spending.

insights.claim: Federal hybrid classical-quantum systems require domestic infrastructure, US personnel, and encrypted links with managed certificates, and the federal acquisition workforce needs training on buying and deploying quantum.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Sovereignty requirements favor US-domiciled providers and create demand for acquisition education.
insights.locator: In the federal sector, these security upgrades

insights.claim: CGI Federal measures success by 'Mission Return on Investment', meaning lower execution costs and faster delivery, rather than standard profit-and-loss metrics.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Government quantum sales hinge on mission-outcome framing rather than financial ROI.
